findings.title: Amount formatting assumes every currency has 2 decimal places
findings.explanation: `Number(invoice.amount) / 100` and `toFixed(2)` are wrong for zero-decimal currencies such as JPY and for three-decimal currencies such as KWD. This is a document for accounting teams, so a wrong amount is a real defect. Reuse the formatting helper that `serializeInvoice` or the rest of the app uses, or use `Intl.NumberFormat` with the currency's minor-unit exponent. Also confirm that `amount` is an integer minor-unit column, and that it cannot exceed safe-integer range if it is a bigint.

findings.title: Date formatting through toISOString can shift the day
findings.explanation: If `period_start` and `period_end` are `DATE` columns, node-pg parses them as local-midnight `Date` objects. `toISOString()` converts to UTC, so on a server whose timezone is ahead of UTC the printed date is one day early. If the columns are `timestamptz`, the UTC date may differ from the customer's billing date. Either cast in SQL (`to_char(i.period_start, 'YYYY-MM-DD')` or `i.period_start::text`) or configure the pg date parser to return strings. Also decide whether `period_end` is inclusive or exclusive, since the printed range says 'to'. Nullable columns would throw on `.toISOString()`.

findings.title: 'Amount due' is misleading for paid or void invoices
findings.explanation: The label is hard-coded, so a paid, void or refunded invoice still says 'Amount due: X'. An accounting team could read that as an outstanding balance. Use 'Amount' or 'Total', or vary the label by status.

findings.title: Status and currency are interpolated into HTML without escaping
findings.explanation: `org_name` is escaped but `invoice.status` and `invoice.currency` are not. They are probably constrained values today, so this is not exploitable now. If either column ever becomes free-form, or an enum gains an unexpected value, it becomes stored XSS. Escape every interpolated value (`escapeHtml(String(...))`) so the template is safe by construction.

findings.title: Non-numeric or non-integer invoiceId causes a DB error instead of a 404
findings.explanation: `Number('abc')` is `NaN` and `Number('1.5')` is 1.5. Either is sent to an integer column and Postgres raises `invalid input syntax`, which surfaces as a 500. Validate with `Number.isInteger(id) && id > 0` and return 404 or 400. Very large values can also overflow int4. Ideally share one param-parsing helper with the existing `/:invoiceId` route.

findings.title: Async handler has no error handling
findings.explanation: If this repo runs Express 4, a rejected `pool.query` in an async handler is not passed to the error middleware. The result is an unhandled rejection and a request that hangs. Wrap the handler in try/catch, or use the project's async wrapper if the existing routes have one.

findings.title: Missing response headers for a sensitive printable document
findings.explanation: Consider `Cache-Control: private, no-store` so shared proxies and browsers do not cache financial data. Consider `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a restrictive CSP (`default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'`) as defense in depth for an HTML response built from DB data. If the intent is 'download', consider `Content-Disposition`, or at least add print-friendly markup (`<html>`, `<meta charset>`, `<title>`, basic print CSS).

findings.title: Confirm auth and role checks match the other invoice routes
findings.explanation: The org scoping (`i.org_id = $2` from `req.user.orgId`) is correct and the query is parameterized. I could not see the router setup. Confirm that auth middleware applies at the router level, so `req.user` is never undefined here, and that any billing-role or permission check on the existing invoice routes also covers this one.

findings.title: Duplicated helper and missing tests
findings.explanation: `escapeHtml` is defined locally, so check whether a shared utility or templating library already exists. The PR adds no tests. Add at least cases for a cross-org invoice returning 404, a nonexistent id, HTML escaping of the org name, and date and amount formatting.

prompt:
Review this pull request. ## Add printable invoice download Customers want a printable copy of an invoice for their accounting team. Adds `GET /invoices/:invoiceId/print`, which returns a simple HTML invoice. Scoped to the caller's organization like the other invoice routes. ## Diff ```diff diff --git a/src/routes/invoices.ts b/src/routes/invoices.ts index 938fffd..04598f2 100644 --- a/src/routes/invoices.ts +++ b/src/routes/invoices.ts @@ -39,3 +39,25 @@ invoicesRouter.get('/:invoiceId', async (req, res) => { if (!rows[0]) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'not_found' }) res.json(serializeInvoice(rows[0])) }) + +invoicesRouter.get('/:invoiceId/print', async (req, res) => { + const { rows } = await pool.query( + `SELECT i.id, i.amount, i.currency, i.status, i.period_start, i.period_end, o.name AS org_name + FROM invoices i JOIN organizations o ON o.id = i.org_id + WHERE i.id = $1 AND i.org_id = $2`, + [Number(req.params.invoiceId), req.user.orgId], + ) + const invoice = rows[0] + if (!invoice) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'not_found' }) + const amount = (Number(invoice.amount) / 100).toFixed(2) + res.type('html').send(` +

Invoice #${invoice.id}

+

${escapeHtml(invoice.org_name)}

+

Period: ${invoice.period_start.toISOString().slice(0, 10)} to ${invoice.period_end.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}

+

Amount due: ${amount} ${invoice.currency.toUpperCase()}

+

Status: ${invoice.status}

`) +}) + +function escapeHtml(value: string): string { + return value.replace(/[&<>"']/g, (c) => ({ '&': '&', '<': '<', '>': '>', '"': '"', "'": ''' })[c] as string) +} ``` Before answering, check the change specifically for: authorization and tenant isolation; race conditions and concurrent requests; database migration safety on large tables and during rolling deploys; API changes that break existing clients; retries and idempotency of side effects such as payments; date and time handling; injection; sensitive data in logs; pagination and boundary conditions. Report every problem you would raise in a code review, from blocking issues to nits. Respond with only a JSON object, no prose before or after it: {"findings": [{"file": "path/to/file", "line": , "severity": "blocking" | "non-blocking" | "nit", "title": "", "explanation": ""}]} Use an empty findings list if you would approve the pull request as it is. Write the review in English.
